questions.prompt: A probability can be any number between...
questions.misconception: Percent form runs 0% to 100%, which maps to 0 to 1 — negative or extra-large chances are not possible.

questions.prompt: On a 4-sided spinner, what is the probability of landing on 3?
questions.explanation: One good sector out of four equal sectors: 1 ÷ 4 = 1/4.
questions.misconception: It is the event's ways over the total ways — 1 wants out of 4, not 3 or 2.

questions.prompt: What is the probability of an IMPOSSIBLE event?
questions.misconception: 1 is certainty, 0.5 is an even bet — impossible is placed all the way at 0.

questions.prompt: You spin a fair 4-sided spinner 400 times. About how many 3s do you expect?
questions.explanation: Each spin has a 1/4 chance: 400 × 1/4 = about 100 on average.
questions.misconception: It is about 100, not exactly — chance wanders a little, but 1/4 of 400 is the best prediction.

questions.prompt: With very many trials, experimental probability...
questions.explanation: The averages of many trials pull toward the calculated theoretical value.
questions.misconception: The experiment wobbles at low trials but converges near the true chance as trials increase — it never grows or shrinks arbitrarily.
